label: Confirmed Cases (2026 DRC + Uganda + France)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / CIDRAP — 16–17 August 2026
contestNote: DRC: 4,945 confirmed across 55 of 151 health zones in 6 provinces (Ituri 4,194, North Kivu 596, Haut-Uélé 138, Tshopo 13, South Kivu 3, Bas-Uélé 1) as of 15 August, published 16 August. Uganda's outbreak was declared officially over 28 July 2026 (20 confirmed, 18 recoveries, 2 deaths). France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. WHO estimates true DRC case count could be up to 4x higher than reported given ongoing active transmission and community mistrust limiting detection.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed cases roughly thirteenfold since early June: 400 (June 5) → 2,011 (July 15) → 3,605 (July 30) → 4,053 (August 5) → 4,665 (August 13) → 4,945 (August 16). This is now the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide, behind only the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases). Africa CDC warns it could become the largest ever recorded if not slowed.

label: Lab-Confirmed Cases (2026 Outbreak — DRC + Uganda + France)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / CIDRAP — 16–17 August 2026
deltaNote: The 16 August DRC situation report recorded an increase of 101 confirmed cases and 53 deaths from the prior day alone (89 Ituri, 8 North Kivu, 3 Haut-Uélé, 1 Tshopo). 730 patients currently hospitalized in isolation in DRC; 1,040 recovered. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the outbreak 'is already the second-biggest Ebola epidemic on record, and it's moving faster than any previous Ebola outbreak.'

label: Deaths (2026 Outbreak)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / CIDRAP — 16–17 August 2026
contestNote: Confirmed deaths: 2,325 DRC + 2 Uganda = 2,327 total as of 15 August, published 16 August. CFR (confirmed): ~47% (2,325/4,945 DRC). The toll surpassed the 2,299 deaths of DRC's 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak, making this the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history — deaths rose from 1,000 to 2,000 in under a month, the fastest fatal surge in Ebola's recorded history. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher said the outbreak was killing one person every 30 minutes as of 14 August. WHO reports 60–70% of deaths occur in communities away from treatment centers.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed deaths: 64 (June 5) → 754 (July 15) → 1,587 (July 30) → 1,850 (August 5) → 2,184 (August 13) → 2,325 (August 16). 155 confirmed cases among healthcare workers, 45 deaths (29% CFR among HCWs).

label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / CIDRAP — 16–17 August 2026
contestNote: Crude CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; DRC's CFR has climbed from roughly 20% in early June to ~47% by mid-August as the outbreak has spread into less-accessible, less-resourced health zones across a sixth province (Bas-Uélé). BDBV historically 25–47% CFR, but this outbreak's crude CFR now sits at the top of the historical range; CIDRAP and outside experts attribute the rise mainly to strain on the response (late detection, community deaths) rather than a change in virus behavior.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — WHO/DRC Advance Phase 3 Ervebo Trial Talks
value: WHO and DRC advancing talks to launch Phase 3 Ervebo ring trial; could start within ~6 weeks of 7 Aug recommendation
source: STAT News / WHO Technical Advisory Group on Candidate Vaccine Prioritization / Gavi — 7–17 August 2026
contestNote: 7 August: WHO's TAG-CVP recommended prioritizing Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV, licensed for Zaire ebolavirus, ~84% effective against that species) for a Phase 3 trial in DRC to test cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus — not a ring-vaccination design but randomization of individual contacts of cases to vaccine or placebo. 12 August: STAT News reported WHO and DRC authorities advancing trial talks, with Gavi's ~500,000-dose Ervebo stockpile available; WHO said the trial could start roughly six weeks from the TAG-CVP recommendation, pending DRC regulatory/ethics approval, vaccine shipment to Ituri, and team training. As of 17 August the trial had not yet launched. Animal data: 3/4 vaccinated primates survived BDBV challenge vs 1/4 controls; a ferret study showed 100% protection with a research-grade formulation vs 0% in controls. Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV and IAVI's rVSV BDBV remain in earlier-stage human trials and may be added later.
delta: Reversal of 28 May off-label-use ban — Ervebo trial talks now actively advancing, not yet launched
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation and 12 August trial talks are steps toward a structured clinical trial pathway rather than a resumption of off-label ring vaccination.

label: DRC Provinces + Countries Affected
value: 6 DRC provinces (55 health zones) + Uganda (outbreak closed) + France (recovered) + Germany (treated)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / Africa CDC — 16–17 August 2026
delta: 55 of 151 health zones now affected, up from 54 on 13 August
deltaNote: Ituri Province: 4,194 of 4,945 DRC cases (~85%) across 28 of 36 health zones. North Kivu (596 cases, 12/34 zones), Haut-Uélé (138, 6/13), Tshopo (13, 7/23), South Kivu (3, 1/34) and Bas-Uélé (1, 1/11) round out the six affected provinces. Bas-Uélé borders Central African Republic conflict-displacement corridors and has poor road/communications access. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over 28 July. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams. A second WHO IHR Emergency Committee meeting to review PHEIC status was scheduled for 18 August.

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
value: ~85.3% of identified contacts under active follow-up
delta: Coverage improved from ~82.7% (12 August) and ~45% (June) but 60-70% of new cases are still occurring outside monitored contacts
deltaNote: ECDC reported active follow-up at 85.3% of identified contacts as of the 16 August update, up from 82.7% on 10 August — still below the 90%+ threshold needed for rapid suppression. Mercy Corps separately warned 60-70% of new cases are recorded outside monitored contacts, with confirmed cases now just 35km from the South Sudan border. Uganda's contact-tracing program is closed following the 28 July outbreak-end declaration. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone.
